notes: An array shows at most 100 elements then `... n more items`, `-0` prints as `-0` inside a container too, and the column layout measures a full-width glyph as 2 cells and a combining mark as 0 — Node's `getStringWidth` ([ADR-01076](../adr/01/ADR-01076.md))

An object with an omitted optional field prints without that key (`{ name: 'a' }`, not `{ name: 'a', age: undefined }`), a tuple prints like an array (`[ 1, 'a' ]`), and an absent nullable object/tuple field prints its keyword instead of dereferencing null ([ADR-01063](../adr/01/ADR-01063.md))

Multiple arguments are all evaluated before the line is printed (a later argument's own console output can't land mid-line, [ADR-01057](../adr/01/ADR-01057.md)), join with single spaces on one line, a no-arg call prints a bare newline, and `-0` displays as `-0` (Node's util.inspect display; `String(-0)` stays `"0"`) — [ADR-00285](../adr/00/ADR-00285.md)

On Windows, VT/ANSI output processing is enabled on the console at startup (as Node does), so an escape like `\x1b[31m` renders as colour rather than printing literally — no raw mode required ([ADR-00744](../adr/00/ADR-00744.md))

On Windows, the console is set to UTF-8 at startup (restored at exit), so non-ASCII output (`café`, CJK, emoji) renders correctly instead of OEM-code-page mojibake; redirected/piped output is unaffected either way ([ADR-00747](../adr/00/ADR-00747.md))
Writes to stderr, unprefixed — identical to `console.error`, as real Node ([ADR-00285](../adr/00/ADR-00285.md))
`Trace: <message>`, then the program's frames as Node prints them, from the shadow call stack. See [ADR-00166](../adr/00/ADR-00166.md), [ADR-01678](../adr/01/ADR-01678.md).

caveats: An array of objects (columns = the shared fields) or an array of primitives (a single `Values` column) is tabulated; a `columns` filter argument, a plain-object argument, and an array-of-arrays shape aren't tabulated (they fall back to `console.log`, as a non-tabular value does)
notes: Byte-for-byte the same Unicode box-drawing layout as real Node (verified against Node v26) — dynamic per-column width, left-aligned cells sized to the widest entry, quoted string cells ([ADR-00560](../adr/00/ADR-00560.md))
Per-label backing `Map<string, number>` — distinct labels track independent timers, matching real Node. See [ADR-00029](../adr/00/ADR-00029.md), [ADR-00544](../adr/00/ADR-00544.md).

Backed by a real `Map<string, number>`, one count per label; a label is converted with ToString, as Node's `${label}`, and `countReset` of a label with no count is Node's process warning ([ADR-00029](../adr/00/ADR-00029.md), [ADR-01477](../adr/01/ADR-01477.md), [ADR-01495](../adr/01/ADR-01495.md)).
Indents every subsequent `console.*` line by two spaces per nesting level; an unbalanced extra `groupEnd()` floors at depth 0 rather than going negative. See [ADR-00029](../adr/00/ADR-00029.md).

`console.group(...label)` takes variadic label args, formatted like `console.log`; `console.groupCollapsed` is the terminal-identical alias (a browser devtools console would render it collapsed) ([ADR-00792](../adr/00/ADR-00792.md))

caveats: The `colors` option is accepted but ignored — inspected output carries no ANSI here
notes: Prints a single value like a single-argument `console.log`, but with Node's `util.inspect` default nesting depth of **2** (a bare `console.log` uses this compiler's deeper default); the `depth` option overrides it — a literal number caps nesting, `null` is unlimited, and beyond the cap a nested value shows as `[Object]`/`[Array]`, matching Node ([ADR-00583](../adr/00/ADR-00583.md))
